description: I enjoy story telling and researching. I also like to draw anime characters and create animation using an app called Procreate. I am currently in Grade 7 and attend school in Calgary, Alberta.
summary: What happens to a spacecraft after its mission is over? I’m telling the story of the Viking 1 and 2 landers on Mars and the Apollo 11 lunar module on the Moon—spacecraft left behind on other worlds. I created a short, kid-friendly animation with a storytelling app to bring their stories to life and help keep their history from being forgotten.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

My project is an educational YouTube video where I tell the fascinating stories of two abandoned spacecraft in space: the Viking 1 and Viking 2 landers on Mars and the Apollo 11 Lunar Module on the Moon. The video explains their journeys, purposes, important parts and how they helped scientists learn more about space. I use simple explanations and storytelling to make complicated space-related information easier to understand. I also include funny animations and illustrations to make the video more entertaining and keep the audience interested.

2. What benefits does it have?

One of the biggest benefits of my project is that it makes learning about space easier and more enjoyable for younger audiences. Space exploration can sometimes involve complicated scientific words and ideas that are difficult for children to understand. I wanted to change that by explaining the information in simple language without leaving out the important facts. The animations also help viewers picture how the spacecraft worked and make learning more memorable. It combines education and entertainment, allowing children to learn something new while having fun.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

My main goal is to inspire younger children to become curious about space and the amazing discoveries humans have made beyond Earth. I hope that after watching my video, they will feel excited to learn more about planets, spacecraft, astronauts and space exploration. Hopefully, my project will encourage young viewers to ask questions, explore new ideas and perhaps become future scientists, engineers or astronauts!

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use to develop your project?

I used two main applications to create my project: Procreate and CapCut. First, I used Procreate to draw and create all the animations and illustrations myself. I designed the pictures to match the information being explained in the video. Then, I used CapCut to put the animations together, arrange them in the correct order and combine them with the audio and narration. Finally, I uploaded the completed video to YouTube so that other people could watch and learn from it. I did not need any coding languages or special hardware because the project was created using digital drawing and video-editing applications.

5. How is your project creative? What factors did your team consider?

My project is creative because I combined storytelling, digital art, animation and science to turn historical space missions into an entertaining learning experience. I personally drew the animations and illustrations and arranged each picture to match the narration, making sure the visuals helped explain what was being discussed. I also added funny and interesting animations to make the video more enjoyable rather than simply presenting facts on a screen.

While creating the project, I considered my target audience, especially younger children. I wanted to make sure the scientific information was accurate but explained in a way that was easy to follow and understand. I also thought about how to keep viewers interested throughout the video by using colourful drawings, engaging storytelling and humour. My aim was to create something that was not only informative but also fun, creative and inspiring.
